definition: An open standard that lets AI assistants connect to tools and data sources.
exampleSentence: With MCP support, the assistant can read our tickets and documentation directly.

definition: A small program that gives an AI assistant access to one tool or data source through MCP.
exampleSentence: We wrote an MCP server so the assistant can query our internal database.

definition: An AI system that plans steps and uses tools to complete a task by itself.
exampleSentence: The AI agent opened the files, fixed the bug and ran the tests.

definition: Able to work and make decisions without a person controlling every step.
exampleSentence: The new coding assistant can work in autonomous mode for several hours.

definition: A packaged set of instructions and files that teaches an AI agent a specific task.
exampleSentence: We added an agent skill that explains how to deploy our app.

definition: An AI search that reads many sources and writes a detailed report.
exampleSentence: I used deep search to compare five cloud providers before the meeting.

definition: The text you give an AI model to tell it what to do.
exampleSentence: A clear prompt usually gives you a much better answer from the model.

definition: The skill of writing instructions that get good results from AI models.
exampleSentence: Good prompt engineering can save hours of manual editing.

definition: The amount of text an AI model can read and remember at one time.
exampleSentence: The whole codebase did not fit into the model's context window.

definition: A small piece of text, such as part of a word, that an AI model processes.
exampleSentence: Each token costs a small amount of money when you use the API.

definition: When an AI model confidently gives false or invented information.
exampleSentence: Always check the sources, because a hallucination can look very convincing.

definition: Training an existing AI model further on your own data.
exampleSentence: Fine-tuning the model on our support emails improved its answers.

definition: A list of numbers that represents the meaning of a text for an AI system.
exampleSentence: Each document is converted into an embedding before it is stored.

definition: A database that finds information by meaning instead of exact words.
exampleSentence: We store product descriptions in a vector database for smarter search.

definition: A method where an AI model first searches your documents, then answers using them.
exampleSentence: Our chatbot uses RAG to answer questions from the company handbook.

definition: Running a trained AI model to get an answer.
exampleSentence: Inference on a large model needs powerful and expensive GPUs.

definition: Rules that stop an AI system from giving harmful or unwanted answers.
exampleSentence: We added guardrails so the bot never shares customer data.

definition: When an AI model asks to run a function or tool to complete a task.
exampleSentence: With tool calling, the model can check the weather instead of guessing.

definition: An extra working folder linked to the same Git repository, used for another branch.
exampleSentence: I created a second worktree so I could fix a bug without leaving my feature branch.

definition: Temporarily saving unfinished changes in Git so you can switch tasks.
exampleSentence: Use git stash to save your changes before you pull the latest code.

definition: A window where you type text commands to control a computer.
exampleSentence: Open a terminal and type the command to start the server.

definition: The program that reads and runs the commands you type.
exampleSentence: Bash is the default shell on many Linux servers.

definition: Connecting different systems so they can work together.
exampleSentence: The integration with Slack sends a message whenever a build fails.

definition: The overall structure of a software system and how its parts work together.
exampleSentence: The team chose a simple architecture so new developers can understand it quickly.

definition: An approach where an application is built from many small, independent services.
exampleSentence: Moving to microservices let each team deploy its part separately.

definition: One repository that holds the code of many projects.
exampleSentence: All our apps and libraries live in a single monorepo.

definition: A package that holds an application and everything it needs to run anywhere.
exampleSentence: The app runs inside a container, so it works the same on every server.

definition: Automatically managing and coordinating many containers or services.
exampleSentence: Kubernetes handles the orchestration of hundreds of containers in production.

definition: A series of automatic steps that build, test and deploy code.
exampleSentence: The pipeline runs the tests and deploys the app after every merge.

definition: A message one system automatically sends to another when something happens.
exampleSentence: GitHub sends a webhook to our server every time someone pushes code.

definition: A named value set outside the code, such as a password or server address.
exampleSentence: Store the database password in an environment variable, not in the code.

definition: A tool that checks code for errors and style problems.
exampleSentence: The linter warned me about an unused variable in my code.

definition: Improving the structure of code without changing what it does.
exampleSentence: After the refactoring, the code was shorter and easier to test.

definition: Moving your branch's changes on top of the latest version of another branch.
exampleSentence: Please rebase your branch on main before you open the pull request.

definition: Copying one specific commit from one branch to another.
exampleSentence: We decided to cherry-pick the security fix into the old release.

definition: A popular repository manager that stores libraries and build files for a company.
exampleSentence: Our builds download all libraries from the company Nexus server.

definition: A file produced by a build, such as an app package or a library.
exampleSentence: The pipeline uploads the final artifact so testers can download it.

definition: The ability to understand what a system is doing from its logs, metrics and traces.
exampleSentence: Good observability helps us find the cause of slow requests quickly.

definition: A pair of secret files used to log in to servers securely without a password.
exampleSentence: Add your SSH key to GitHub so you can push code without a password.

definition: A secret code that identifies an app when it uses an API.
exampleSentence: Never put your API key in public code on GitHub.
